title: ContextLedgerReplicationBatch
description: An auditable unit of spool -> Evidence Vault replication. A transfer must never be an invisible filesystem side effect: every batch is durable evidence of what moved, when, and whether it verified. Sized so that a NAS outage leaves an explainable queue rather than an unbounded backlog.

batchId.description: Deterministic and sortable, e.g. batch-<ISO8601>-<shortManifestHash>. Stable across retries of the SAME content.

entryCount.description: Number of evidence ledger entries in this batch.

manifestHash.description: sha256 over the canonical batch manifest (the ordered list of contentHash + relative path). Identifies the batch content independent of transport.

localRoot.description: WSL ext4 spool root this batch was drawn from.

remoteRoot.description: Vault root on the NAS, expressed as a registered storage-root id plus path -- NEVER a /mnt/z drvfs path. Machine ingestion must not traverse the Windows mapping.

transport.description: How the bytes actually moved. Recorded so a slow or failed batch is diagnosable after the fact.

identity.description: Service account used, e.g. cg-context-ledger. Never a credential value.

verifiedCount.description: Entries whose REMOTE re-hash equals the local contentHash. Only these may advance to VERIFIED.

failures.description: Never collapsed to a count alone -- a failure must name what did not land.

batchState.description: VERIFIED requires verifiedCount === entryCount AND failedCount === 0. PARTIAL is a real terminal-ish state and must not be reported as success.

integrityEvent.description: Set when a previously VERIFIED object later fails re-hash. A mutated blob is a major integrity event, never a silent new truth.

spoolRetention.description: The local spool copy may only be aged out after remote verification.
